overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violations in any of the twelve complaints. Draft-minute challenges were declined as premature, and the rest were found outside the law or compliant.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged members deliberated outside a posted meeting about removing a disputed email from the May 4 meeting packet.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we find this brief exchange fell within the open Meeting Law’s exception for limited administrative communications and the distribution of meeting information.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the June 1 discussion of a disputed email was not supported by the packet and the email was not made public.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, a failure to include any particular document in a meeting packet in advance of a meeting, or to share documents being discussed with members of the public during a meeting, does not constitute a violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged meeting notices listed disputed emails under Correspondence, making the notices inaccurate.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we do not review the accuracy of the listed correspondence.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the June 29 minutes were inaccurate because they listed a disputed email under Correspondence.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, as explained above, we do not review the accuracy of those minutes.

allegations.summary: Complaints alleged the Board improperly met in executive session in July and August to discuss prior open meeting complaints.
allegations.key_passage: In that determination, we explained that public bodies may meet in executive session in accordance with General Laws Chapter 30A, section 21(a)(1), to discuss Open Meeting Law complaints against the public body.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the July 12 executive session vote was invalid because only two of five members voted, not a majority of the full board.
allegations.key_passage: We do not interpret the Open Meeting Law as requiring that a majority of the full body vote in favor of entering executive session, but rather that a majority of those present and voting must vote in favor of entering executive session.

allegations.summary: Complaints alleged documents were left out of the meeting's official record, for meetings in October through January.
allegations.key_passage: In other words, the Open Meeting Law’s reference to the “official record” of a meeting pertains to the availability of such records if requested under the Public Records Law.

allegations.summary: Complaints about October through January meetings challenged minutes that were not yet approved when the complaints were filed.
allegations.key_passage: we do not review the sufficiency of minutes that were not yet created or that existed only in draft form.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged August 10 minutes inaccurately identified correspondence by unauthenticated sender names without describing content.
allegations.key_passage: We find no violation with regard to the allegedly inaccurate identification of listed documents.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged August 10 minutes did not describe how listed documents were used or attach them.
allegations.key_passage: Likewise, there is no requirement that documents and other exhibits used by a public body be attached to or physically stored with the minutes.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
